selectionEntries.name: About Warsmith's Listbuilder

rules.name: A fancy notepad, not a rules engine
rules.description:
The listbuilder is intended to replace a notepad, not the army rules PDF. It quickly and simply records the choices that make up an army and catches illegal list construction. It does not reproduce every unit rule, weapon profile, or procedural rule from the army rules PDF.

Players are expected to consult the army rules during list construction.

For the core rules and all army rules PDFs, check out the Reforged Discord Server: https://discord.gg/BpjkaNmMVB

rules.name: Not every legal option needs its own button
rules.description:
The listbuilder is intended to make common choices quick, rather than give every legal option equal prominence. Some uncommon or default loadouts may therefore not be represented. Their absence does not make them illegal; the army rules PDF remains authoritative.

When players actually make use of an uncommon option, it can be added accordingly.

selectionEntries.comment: Permanent informational Configuration entry. Player-facing guidance is intentionally condensed to two principles: the listbuilder is a fancy notepad rather than a rules engine, and not every legal option needs its own button. It is inserted by default but intentionally has no min/max constraints because its presence/quantity is not a semantic roster rule.

selectionEntries.name: Game Size

rules.name: Army List - 420 Points
rules.description:
​
Practice is a short rehearsal format for learning your army. Play two battle rounds, then reset and start again. Use the time to practice your army rules, unit abilities, Leader abilities, Attack sequence, and the activation of your core units. Practice is not intended to produce a winner or loser. A Practice session usually takes 30–60 minutes, depending on player experience.

You have one Leader Point.

Each time you bring a unit from the Troops section, if your army list already includes three of that unit, that additional unit costs an additional 20 points.

Each time you bring a unit from the Elites, Transports, or Support sections, that unit costs an additional 20 points.

rules.name: Army List - 800 Points
rules.description:
​
Rapid & lethal - this is the size for quick action. 1-2 hours.

You have two Leader Points.

Each time you bring a unit from the Troops section, if your army list already includes four of that unit, that additional unit costs an additional 20 points.

Each time you bring a unit from the Elites, Transports, or Support sections, if your army list already includes one of that unit, that additional unit costs an additional 20 points.

rules.name: Army List - 1200 Points
rules.description:
​
Bold, tactical play is key at this size as you adapt to the battlefield and the dice. This is the recommended size for 1v1 games. 2-3 hours.

You have three Leader Points.

Each time you bring a unit from the Troops section, if your army list already includes six of that unit, that additional unit costs an additional 20 points.

Each time you bring a unit from the Elites, Transports, or Support sections, if your army list already includes two of that unit, that additional unit costs an additional 20 points.

rules.name: Army List - 1600 Points
rules.description:
​
Strategy takes the spotlight as you battle to extend advantages over the long term. 3+ hours.

You have four Leader Points.

Each time you bring a unit from the Troops section, if your army list already includes eight of that unit, that additional unit costs an additional 20 points.

Each time you bring a unit from the Elites, Transports, or Support sections, if your army list already includes three of that unit, that additional unit costs an additional 20 points.

selectionEntries.comment:
CURRENT GAME SIZE / LEADER POINTS: Game Size is the semantic source of the 420 / 800 / 1200 / 1600 army size and grants 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 Leader Points respectively. Game Size also owns the player-facing Core Rules text for Extra Unit Copy Cost thresholds. Practice is a two-battle-round rehearsal format, then reset. The permanent Leader Points Configuration entry reports the weighted LP budget and overspend state.

POINTS LEGALITY TEST: New Recruit's native Points cost limit remains unlimited (Points defaultCostLimit = -1). Game Size now performs permissive-corrective roster validation against the total Points cost: Practice 420, Quick 800, Standard 1200, Long 1600. Oversized lists remain constructible but produce a corrective error explaining how to return the roster to legality.

GAME SIZE AS GAME MODE / GS38
The Game System exposes four top-level force entries named after the four existing Game Sizes. Choosing a force at roster creation conditionally sets defaultAmount=1 on the matching existing Game Size option. The static selectionEntryGroup defaultSelectionEntryId has been removed for this test. The four Game Size option IDs, Game Size entry ID, Leader Point logic, Extra Unit Copy Cost thresholds, permissive-corrective Points validation, category structure, and downstream catalogue query targets are unchanged. The intended New Recruit behavior is that the chosen top-level Game Mode only seeds the initial Game Size; the Game Size radio selector remains editable afterward. Runtime behavior was verified successfully in New Recruit on September 21st, 2026; this is now the supported GS38 architecture.

gameSystem.comment:
CURRENT STATE — GS38
GS38 formally adopts the runtime-proven Game Size-as-Game-Mode setup and the standardized Configuration order. The four existing Game Size option IDs remain the semantic source for points limits, Leader Points, and copy-cost thresholds. Configuration lanes are 10 Game Size, 40 Leader Points, and 100 About; faction catalogues supply the intervening standardized lanes.

SEMANTIC SOURCE OF TRUTH

The Universal Unit Skeleton (UUS) is the semantic source of truth.

New Recruit is an output format. The compiler MUST NOT invent additional game meaning merely because New Recruit requires a particular data shape.

If a UUS rule cannot be compiled deterministically, fail loudly rather than inventing faction-specific behavior.

Preserve the player's decision structure, not merely the final legality of the roster.

Stable source IDs MUST be preferred wherever they exist. Display names, array positions, and presentation order MUST NOT become surrogate semantic IDs.


GAME SYSTEM ROLE AND AUTHORITY

The Game System is the canonical reusable policy layer for cross-faction listbuilder infrastructure and durable authoring/runtime doctrine.

Reusable concepts belong here when they are genuinely cross-faction:
- canonical shared categories, rules, and Configuration infrastructure;
- proven New Recruit runtime behavior that materially affects authoring;
- reusable authoring and presentation conventions;
- universal validation/error-language patterns;
- shared-library and ID-stability doctrine.

The Game System does NOT own:
- faction-specific game semantics from the UUS or army rules PDF;
- current work-session state, immediate next tasks, or faction progress;
- routine audit/update procedure owned by the Catalogue Maintenance & Presentation Guide;
- historical archaeology that no longer explains current behavior.

When a catalogue experiment establishes a genuinely reusable pattern, promote the durable lesson here once it is proven. Do not promote an untested hypothesis merely because it looks elegant or worked in one unusually specific structure.

If a Game System comment conflicts with current executable Game System data, the executable data wins. If theoretical expectations conflict with observed New Recruit runtime behavior, the observed runtime behavior wins.


CATEGORY ARCHITECTURE

New Recruit categories MUST NOT be treated as the semantic source of unit identity.

Categories are divided into two classes:

Presentation Categories

Visible to the player.
May be used as primary categories.
Determine organization in the New Recruit builder.
MUST NOT be relied upon for list-building semantics.

Internal Semantic Categories

Used only where New Recruit requires or benefits from grouping multiple semantic objects.
MUST be hidden from the player where possible.
MUST NOT be primary categories.
MUST NOT determine where a unit appears in the builder.
MUST describe genuine reusable semantic sets, not one-off implementation accidents.

Prefer direct stable-ID references over creating an internal category when a rule refers to specific named objects.

Attachment behavior MUST be represented through attachment/Association semantics, not inferred from presentation category.

Unit limits MUST derive from UUS semantic fields such as unit_class, counts_toward_unit_type_limit, restrictions and list-building effects, not from the unit's visible New Recruit category.


GAME SIZE AND POINTS LIMITS

The New Recruit Points cost type MUST have no preselected roster cost limit.

Players MUST NOT be required to specify an army points limit when creating a roster.

The Points cost type therefore uses an unlimited/default limit (-1).

For Create List presentation, Points uses normal always-visible Game System behavior. LP is hidden before the roster force exists and restored once the live force is present, removing the generic LP Cost Limit input without suppressing its normal in-roster display.

Army size is selected after roster creation through the mandatory Game Size configuration choice.

The available Game Size options are:

420 Points (Practice)
800 Points (Quick)
1200 Points (Standard)
1600 Points (Long)

The selected Game Size is the semantic source of all game-size-dependent list-building restrictions, including army-size rules, unit-copy costs and Leader Point budgets.

The generic New Recruit roster cost-limit field MUST NOT be treated as authoritative game-size information.

If a dynamic roster-points ceiling cannot be represented reliably in New Recruit, do not fake it. Keep Game Size as the semantic source and leave the generic Points limit unlimited until the mechanic is proven.


LISTBUILDER PRESENTATION PHILOSOPHY

The listbuilder is a companion to the army rules PDF and a fancy notepad, not a replacement rules engine.

Represent the choices players actually make when recording an army.

Do not reproduce procedural replacement wording merely because the PDF expresses a final loadout through a sequence of "replace X with Y" instructions.

Prefer a direct final-state choice when it preserves the real list-building decision.

The common 99% path SHOULD be quick and obvious. Exceptional edge cases may rely on the army rules PDF when reproducing them would materially worsen the list-building interface.

When there is tension between literal procedural wording and a clean exact representation of the final choice, prefer the clean exact representation.

Do not hide point costs or create invisible taxes. Any points added by the builder MUST remain visible to the player.

During presentation or maintenance work, prefer labels, wrappers, ordering, grouping, and error-message improvements over mechanical redesign.

Do not redesign a functioning mechanical structure merely because it looks unconventional in JSON. Change mechanics only when the current structure causes a real player-facing problem, violates current source semantics, or a mechanical correction is explicitly intended.

Current executable behavior and observed New Recruit runtime behavior take precedence over stale authoring comments or historical implementation notes.


UI SHAPE AND SEMANTIC VALIDATION ARE SEPARATE CONCERNS

The New Recruit object that records a player choice does not need to be the same object that enforces every rule governing that choice.

Choose the simplest exact player-facing input shape first. If a stock min/max constraint, association cap, or other built-in validator makes the interface awkward or exposes implementation vocabulary, semantic legality MAY be enforced separately with a constructive custom validator.

Stock constraints are implementation tools, not sacred project doctrine.

Removing or relaxing a stock constraint is acceptable only when the same game-rule legality remains enforced elsewhere. A cleaner UI MUST NOT silently become a more permissive rules implementation.

When a separate validator is used, prefer player-facing game language and the established three-part corrective pattern where appropriate.


UNIT ORDERING AND PLAYER-FACING NAMES

Root units MUST appear in the same order as their army rules PDF unless a specific design decision says otherwise. Use stable Position/sortIndex values to preserve this order.

Use the proper in-universe model or role name whenever one exists.

For infantry model groups, prefer:
1. Proper role/title, such as Sister Superior, Exarch, Justicar, Klaivex, Shas'vre.
2. Faction-specific model noun.
3. Singular/plural unit model noun.
4. Generic "Model N" only as an absolute fallback.

A sergeant/champion occupies the first model position for numbering purposes. If a unit contains a named sergeant followed by numbered models, the next ordinary model is Model 2, not Model 1.

Do not invent a sergeant title when the unit has no distinct sergeant loadout to record.

Unit roots use the ordinary ▸ unit-row marker. Do not add catalogue-owned medal/badge emoji to commander or command-tier unit names. Command status belongs in actual listbuilding semantics such as Leader Points, restrictions, attachments, and rules, not decorative name badges.


LOADOUT UI GRAMMAR

The listbuilder should make three questions easy to answer at a glance:
1. What am I looking at?
2. Which model or model-group does this choice belong to?
3. What is that model or group equipped with?

Use explicit model or model-group headers when they materially improve clarity. Do not invent a canonical model noun when the source does not establish one.

Use these top-level section names consistently when they genuinely describe the player's decision:
- Loadout Options
- Paid Wargear
- Additional Model
- Attached [MODEL / LEADER]
- Unit Upgrade / Mutation Upgrade / Protocol Upgrade / other specific semantic upgrade heading

Do not use "Special Weapon Loadouts" merely as catalogue taxonomy. Specialist models and special weapons normally belong inside ordinary Loadout Options unless the enclosing branch represents a genuine mutually exclusive structural choice.

Do not use generic "Additional Leader" as player-facing relationship text when the actual nested model or Leader has a meaningful identity. Prefer relationship names such as Attached Imagifier, Attached Lhamaean, or Attached Plasmacyte.

Omit sections that do not apply.

Mandatory exclusive choices SHOULD normally use min 1 / max 1 and default to the first normal/legal option.

Do NOT create a default if doing so can open the unit in an illegal state. In that case, prefer an optional 0/1 presentation with a built-in (None) state and validate completion separately with a constructive custom error.

Fixed equipment may be represented as a one-option mandatory group when displaying it materially improves the recorded loadout.

Physical slot labels such as Left Arm, Right Arm, Weapon 1, Weapon 2, Shoulder Weapon 1, or Heavy Weapon 2 SHOULD be omitted when the slot identity has no rules consequence and only narrates the implementation.

Physical slot labels MAY be retained when they explain a real dependency, physical choice, or meaningful equipment category, such as Main Weapon, Coaxial Weapon, or Sidearm.

Do not add invisible wrapper groups merely to force a particular collapse/indentation behavior. Empty visual wrappers have previously produced blank gaps and poor New Recruit UI.

Zero-width group labels MAY be used to suppress a redundant visible header while retaining the structural object, stable ID, default, legality, or other semantics owned by that group.


ATOMIC PACKAGES AND FINAL-STATE READABILITY

When multiple pieces of equipment are inseparable as one selectable final-state package, present the whole package as one selection and join its components with " & ".

Do not use " + " for atomic packages. "+" reads like arithmetic or separate recorded selections rather than one inseparable loadout.

When several atomic packages share the same component, place the differentiating or meaningful component first when doing so improves scanability.

Example:
Reaper Autocannon & Bubotic Weapon
is generally clearer than:
Bubotic Weapon & Reaper Autocannon

Do not mechanically reorder every package. Apply meaningful-choice-first only where a repeated shared component obscures the real decision.

When one component is always present and the player is genuinely choosing only another component, split the fixed component from the choice into separate visible lines if doing so is mechanically safe.

Do not split an atomic package when one branch replaces the whole package and the split would require brittle conditional mandatory groups, selected-hidden behavior, fake "No Weapon" choices, or other implementation complexity.

Standardise the visual grammar, but do not force unlike rules into identical shapes. Individual consideration beats blind standardisation when an unusual label or structure directly communicates a real source distinction.

SERGEANTS, CHAMPIONS AND SPECIALIST MODELS

When a sergeant/champion has a distinct loadout, represent that model directly under its proper title and place it first.

Do not pretend a sergeant/champion starts as an ordinary model and then "upgrades" into its actual equipment.

If a free specialist replacement is effectively the intended identity of a model slot, represent that specialist directly and omit ordinary fallback equipment when the fallback would only advertise a non-meaningful choice.

If the specialist option costs points, retain the ordinary fallback state because declining the paid upgrade is a meaningful list-building choice.

When the source allows up to X specialist selections and repetition is allowed, prefer X independent model/choice slots over a quantity spinner.

Prefer structural prevention of a unit-wide cap only when the prevention remains local, clear, and cannot hide an already-selected state.

Do not use cross-model hiding merely to avoid a corrective validation error when doing so makes the structure brittle or risks selected-hidden invalid states.

When clean prevention is not available, keep the valid input choices visible and use permissive-corrective validation to explain and repair the illegal combination.

Conditional hiding MUST NOT create a state where an already-selected option later becomes hidden. New Recruit treats selected-hidden entries as invalid.


PAID WARGEAR

Paid Wargear is for additive equipment or abilities whose ownership does not need to be tracked on a specific physical model.

If taking the option requires a model to lose or replace existing equipment, the paid option belongs inline on the affected model's loadout, not as unit-level Paid Wargear.

Unmodelled additive wargear, grenades, cherubs, smoke launchers, icons, bombs and similar unit-level bookkeeping SHOULD normally be represented at unit level.

A single independent optional paid item SHOULD normally be a direct upgrade selection with a max-1 constraint. New Recruit renders this proven shape as a checkbox-style control.

Do not introduce a one-item optional wrapper group merely to force checkbox presentation.

If several mutually exclusive paid items occupy one choice, an optional max-1 group with no minimum may be used; New Recruit can expose an empty radio state for the unselected option.

If a unit may take the same class of paid upgrade multiple times and model identity is not important, prefer multiple independent optional slots rather than a quantity spinner.

If model identity matters, place the paid option inline on the eligible model slots.

Ability-only paid wargear MUST include the full exact player-facing ability text on the selection.


UNIT ABILITY PROFILE OWNERSHIP

The reusable profile type 🏷️ Unit Abilities contains top-level ability names only. Nested/sub-abilities are not represented unless they independently exist as a top-level ability elsewhere.

A top-level ability that is intrinsic to the datasheet is linked from the unit root.

A top-level ability granted only by a selectable upgrade, wargear item, mode, or mandatory choice MUST be linked from the selection that actually grants it, not from the unit root. This keeps the Profiles section aligned with the player's current final-state selection.

If several independent selectable objects can each grant the same ability, reuse the same shared ability Profile and give each granting selection its own infoLink. Do not duplicate the shared Profile merely to support multiple grantors.

Mandatory fixed equipment remains root-linked when the ability is always present and the apparent equipment selection is only structural presentation.

Audit ability ownership semantically. Do not move a profile merely because an optional item has a similar name; verify that the selectable item actually grants the top-level ability.


RULE TEXT AUTHORING

When player-facing rule text is available in the authoritative army rules PDF, preserve it verbatim.

Do not paraphrase attachment wording, Leader Point wording, or ability-only wargear text when the exact wording is available.

If exact wording is unavailable, do not invent a synthetic rule and present it as authoritative.

Rules that are already fully represented by a weapon/profile name do not need their full weapon mechanics duplicated in the listbuilder.

The listbuilder SHOULD include full text for selections whose mechanical identity is primarily a named ability rather than a weapon/profile.


VARIABLE UNIT SIZE

When practical, represent the minimum legal unit size in the root unit cost and add larger sizes through Additional Models.

Additional models SHOULD be explicit model entries with their own point cost and loadout subtree when they have meaningful individual choices.

Avoid quantity spinners for additional models when a clearer model-entry presentation is available.

For an optional max-one additional model, retain the structural wrapper when it carries useful hierarchy or nesting, but place the max-1 constraint on the direct type:model child. New Recruit renders this proven shape as a checkbox-style Additional Model control.

Sequential/nested optional additional-model entries MAY be used when extra models are identical and nesting produces a clearer 4/5/6-style progression than a quantity control.

Dynamically revealed additional models that themselves contain mandatory/default child selectors MUST be runtime-tested. New Recruit does not always instantiate a newly revealed mandatory/default child selector exactly as expected.

Do not leave a Phase 0.1 minimum-size shell comment once proper variable-size controls have been implemented.


ATTACHMENTS AND NESTED LEADERS

Normal Leaders that must join a host SHOULD use the established Association pattern:
- Leader-side association min 0 / max 1.
- Eligible host units carry hidden "May Attach To: X" semantic categories.
- A constructive Leader-side missing-attachment error enforces the requirement.
- Eligible hosts own their attachment-capacity validation and use player-facing corrective errors rather than stock implementation-language errors.

Every Leader SHOULD also display the exact player-facing attachment rule text from the PDF.

A Countless or host-local Leader that is conceptually selected as part of its host MAY use a nested attached-Leader pattern instead of appearing as a floating root Leader.

When that nested relationship is player-facing, name it for the actual model or role, such as Attached Imagifier or Attached Lhamaean, rather than exposing a generic implementation label such as Additional Leader.

The nested attached-Leader pattern is especially appropriate when:
- the Leader does not spend Leader Points,
- the Leader may coexist with a normal attached Leader,
- and there is no meaningful reason for the player to select the Leader before selecting its host.

Nested Leader units retain their own complete unit/loadout tree.

Nested units may themselves be valid association targets. This has been proven and may be used when it makes the roster easier to understand.

When a rule grants required/free child units, a Neuroloid-style nested generated unit is preferred over asking the player to create and then associate the granted unit manually, provided the nested child remains fully configurable.


EXTRA UNIT COPY COSTS

The Game System owns the reusable semantic categories and shared player-facing rules for Extra Unit Copy Costs.

The catalogue owns per-unit arithmetic because copy counting references catalogue-local unit IDs.

The generic soft-copy-cost system has two parallel copy families:

Troop units:
- 420 Points (Practice): first 3 copies cost normal points.
- 800 Points (Quick): first 4 copies cost normal points.
- 1200 Points (Standard): first 6 copies cost normal points.
- 1600 Points (Long): first 8 copies cost normal points.

Other units:
- 420 Points (Practice): no copies are exempt from the surcharge.
- 800 Points (Quick): first 1 copy costs normal points.
- 1200 Points (Standard): first 2 copies cost normal points.
- 1600 Points (Long): first 3 copies cost normal points.

Each additional identical copy costs +20 Points.

Copy allowances are per datasheet/copy-family, not pooled across the entire Troop or Other presentation category. Rare units retain their hard max-1 rule unless source semantics say otherwise.

Affected Troop units use the hidden Counts Toward Troop Soft Copy Cost semantic category. Affected Other units use the hidden Counts Toward Other Soft Copy Cost semantic category. Affected units link the appropriate shared reminder rule.

Each catalogue owns one permanent required Extra Unit Copy Costs Configuration entry. It is a single flat visible accounting item. Do not recreate visible Troops / Other ledger children. Keep separate internal modifiers for Troop and Other arithmetic as needed.

Practice Troop accounting preserves the same +20-per-extra-copy model with the normal allowance reduced to 3. Practice Other applies +20 beginning with the first eligible Other copy.

Never apply a surcharge invisibly to unit costs in a way the player cannot identify.

A separate accounting Configuration does not reliably expose every association-count state in New Recruit. Where source semantics guarantee a one-to-one mapping between the relevant association state and a countable selection state, a selection-count proxy MAY be used for arithmetic or refund logic. Document the semantic guarantee and runtime-test the result.


ERROR MESSAGE AUTHORING CONVENTION

Prefer structurally preventing an illegal choice when that can be done without making the interface harder to understand.

If structural prevention would make the interface awkward, brittle, or capable of hiding an already-selected choice, keep the cleaner input shape and validate the illegal state separately.

Custom validation errors MUST use player-facing game terminology. Do not expose New Recruit implementation vocabulary such as association, selection, constraint, child, or parent.

The three-part corrective pattern is preferred for permissive-corrective validation:

1. State the invalid condition.
2. State the allowed condition.
3. State the repair.

Proven example:

"This unit has more than one Painboy attached. It may have only one Painboy attached. Remove or move one of the attached Painboys."

Templates are guidance, not rigid strings. Natural wording appropriate to the specific rule takes priority over mechanically filling placeholders.

REUSABLE SHARED UNIT CONTENT

When complete playable unit trees are reused across multiple armies, compile a dedicated shared library and use thin host-specific entryLinks.

Do not duplicate the full unit tree into every host catalogue merely because New Recruit permits it.

Do not import an entire playable faction catalogue when only reusable unit content is needed.

The shared compiled library is still an output artifact. The UUS remains the semantic source of truth.

The shared library owns intrinsic unit-tree content: unit-local loadouts, costs, rules, unit-internal validation, attachment associations, and reusable semantic categories.

The consumer catalogue owns host-specific availability, Configuration gating, primary presentation category, consumer-local eligibility/attachment semantics, and catalogue-local accounting such as Extra Unit Copy Costs.

Consumer-specific semantics SHOULD normally be applied to the consumer entryLink or other consumer-local object rather than written back into the reusable shared unit tree.

Do not rebuild or bump a linked shared library when the consumer-only implementation changes and the shared unit tree itself is unchanged.

Verify the actual linked library's ID, display name, revision, and Game System target before synchronizing a human-readable catalogueLink label.

New Recruit may export the canonical name of a shared target rather than a consumer entryLink's local display-name override. When export wording matters, keep the shared target's canonical name suitable for export rather than relying on the local override.


PROVEN NEW RECRUIT UI / RUNTIME BEHAVIOR

The following behaviors are proven enough to guide implementation, but runtime testing remains authoritative when a new structure combines them in an unfamiliar way.

Promote a New Recruit behavior into reusable doctrine only after it has been observed in New Recruit or otherwise directly verified. Untested engine assumptions MUST remain hypotheses, and the required runtime test should be stated explicitly rather than presented as fact.

- Direct optional upgrade selection + max 1 renders as a checkbox-style control.
- A retained structural wrapper containing one direct type:model child with max 1 on the model renders as a checkbox-style Additional Model control.
- Optional max-1 radio groups with no minimum and no default can expose a visible empty radio state.
- Zero-width group labels can suppress redundant visible headers while preserving the underlying group, ID, default, and legality.
- Selected-hidden states are invalid and must be avoided.
- Dynamically revealed mandatory/default child selectors may require runtime testing because New Recruit does not always instantiate the newly revealed default exactly as expected.
- Local entryLink display names may differ from the canonical shared target name used in exports.
- Catalogue-local Association counts are not always visible from a separate accounting Configuration; use a semantically guaranteed selection-count proxy only when the mapping is exact and documented.
- A custom secondary cost type is displayed alongside Points on selections that carry a positive value.
- Roster-scope conditions can query the accumulated total of a custom secondary cost type by using that cost type ID as the condition field.
- A permanent Configuration entry can use those cost-total conditions to report a live remaining / maximum resource counter.
- In the tested Leader Points structures, nested and imported/shared selections contribute their intrinsic LP cost exactly once.
- A cost type may be hidden during roster creation and restored inside the finished roster by setting the cost type hidden by default and conditionally setting hidden=false once the live force exists. This is runtime-proven for both Points and LP and removes their generic Cost Limits inputs from Create List without suppressing their normal in-roster display.
- A force entry's visible name may be a zero-width character while retaining the force ID, categories, validation, and roster semantics. This suppresses the otherwise redundant single-force label in the roster UI. Setting forceEntry.hidden=true does not suppress that rendered label and is not a substitute for the zero-width-name presentation pattern.


PREFER DIRECT REPRESENTATION OVER ARTIFICIAL CODIFICATION

The compiler MUST choose the simplest exact New Recruit representation for each semantic rule.

Repeated local constraints, conditions, modifiers, or explicit unit references are acceptable, even when they occur on many objects.

Shared categories, tags, helper entries, or other abstractions SHOULD be introduced only when they represent a meaningful reusable concept or materially simplify the resulting implementation.

The number of objects affected is not, by itself, a reason to create or avoid an abstraction.

Do not create a keyword merely because several objects happen to share the same implementation.

Do not duplicate logic merely because only one object currently uses an existing meaningful concept.

Prefer whichever representation has fewer dependencies, less indirection, and clearer correspondence to the UUS semantics.


CATALOGUE DATA AUTHORING CONVENTION: DETERMINISTIC IDS

All AI-authored or compiler-generated catalogue objects MUST use deterministic IDs.

ID algorithm

Construct the object's canonical semantic path.
Canonical paths MUST describe semantic identity, never array position, display order, or other incidental structure.
Where stable source IDs exist, such as UUS unit IDs, model-group IDs, selection-group IDs, option IDs, or configuration IDs, those IDs MUST be used in the canonical path rather than display names.
The path MUST identify the object type and enough semantic ancestry to uniquely identify the object.
Convert the complete path to lowercase.
Use / as the separator.
Hash the UTF-8 path using SHA-256.
Take the first 16 hexadecimal characters.
Format as xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx.

Existing IDs of live semantic objects are authoritative and MUST NOT be regenerated merely because an object's name, presentation, or surrounding structure changes.
References to live objects MUST reuse their existing IDs.
Only genuinely new catalogue objects receive deterministic IDs.
Every distinct live object MUST have exactly one distinct canonical semantic path.
Compiler-generated helper objects MUST use paths describing their semantic purpose, not numeric counters or creation order.
Renaming or moving a live object does NOT automatically change its ID.
If two distinct objects produce the same canonical path, compilation MUST fail.
If two different canonical paths produce the same deterministic ID, compilation MUST fail.
Never resolve references by display name when an ID exists.
Never generate random IDs for AI-authored or compiler-generated catalogue data.


ID STABILITY AND OBSOLETE OBJECTS

ID stability protects meaningful live semantic continuity. It does not require retaining obsolete implementation objects.

Duplicate, superseded, unreachable, or otherwise unused objects MAY be deleted when their removal does not:
- break an existing live reference;
- erase meaningful semantic continuity;
- break compatibility with a deliberately preserved live selection.

Before deleting an object, verify that no live targetId, childId, defaultSelectionEntryId, category reference, modifier, constraint, association, or other semantic reference depends on it.

A legacy shell MAY be retained when it serves an identified compatibility or migration purpose. It SHOULD NOT be retained solely because the object once had an ID.

Preserve IDs because the object still matters, not because the ID once existed.


GAME SYSTEM ID STABILITY

Game System IDs do not need to be regenerated deterministically.

Once a Game System object is adopted into the canonical system, its ID is authoritative and MUST remain stable because faction catalogues may reference it.

New AI-authored Game System objects MAY use deterministic IDs as a safe default, but deterministic regeneration of existing Game System IDs is not required or desired.


FUTURE SHARED CONTENT CATEGORIES

The Game System defines visible presentation categories for:
- Great Traitors’ Arsenal
- Left Hand of the Emperor
- Space Marines Vehicles
- Astra Militarum Vehicles
- Black Legion
- Iron Warriors
- Night Lords
- Alpha Legion
- Ultramarines
- Blood Angels
- Space Wolves
- Salamanders

These categories are presentation infrastructure only. They do not independently define eligibility, copy limits, attachment rules, import behavior, or any other game semantics. Consumer catalogues and linked shared libraries own the actual availability and unit semantics.


ABOUT WARSMITH'S LISTBUILDER

The Game System owns a permanent About Warsmith's Listbuilder Configuration entry.

It is positioned before Game Size and is intended to remain visible in every faction catalogue that uses this Game System.

This entry is player-facing guidance. It MUST NOT become a semantic source for compiler behavior.


COMMENT AND REVISION HYGIENE

Game System and catalogue comments are authoring documentation.

Use comments to record durable conventions, implementation rationale, known engine behavior, and intentional simplifications.

Prefer recording reusable standards in the Game System comment and unit/faction-specific exceptions in catalogue or unit comments.

Do not duplicate large generic conventions into every catalogue.

Do not preserve obsolete comments, legacy shells, or dead helper objects merely as historical archaeology. Keep historical notes only when they explain current behavior, a live compatibility requirement, or a deliberate exception.

A comment-only documentation change does not require a Game System revision bump.

Bump the Game System revision when a referenced Game System object, rule, category, force structure, cost type, or other executable/player-visible Game System data changes.


CONFIGURATION VALIDATION PATTERNS

Purely informational Configuration entries that are inserted by default, such as About Warsmith's Listbuilder, SHOULD NOT carry min/max constraints when their absence or duplication does not change roster legality.

Semantic/accounting Configuration entries are different: if their quantity affects points or legality, they MUST remain protected against accidental deletion or duplication, preferably with constructive custom errors rather than stock New Recruit implementation-language errors.

Game Size and Extra Unit Copy Costs are universal examples. Missing required Configuration validation belongs at a durable shared parent such as Army > Configuration when that lets the Game System provide one clear player-facing repair message.

Subfaction Configuration validation uses reusable opt-in semantics. A catalogue that uses Regiment, Legion, or Chapter terminology marks a durable Configuration entry with Uses Regiment / Uses Legion / Uses Chapter and marks the actual selector with Required Subfaction Configuration. Army > Configuration then reports the corresponding missing-selector error only for catalogues that opt into that system.


LEADER POINTS

Leader Points are an expendable army-list resource represented by the canonical secondary cost type LP ⭐.

Game Size grants the Leader Point budget:
- 420 Points (Practice): 1 Leader Point.
- 800 Points (Quick): 2 Leader Points.
- 1200 Points (Standard): 3 Leader Points.
- 1600 Points (Long): 4 Leader Points.

A selection that spends Leader Points carries a positive LP cost directly on its semantic owner. A selection without an LP cost spends no Leader Points; do not add synthetic 0 LP costs.

The roster-wide LP total is the mathematical source of Leader Point expenditure. Game Size owns the universal overspend validator and reports a constructive player-facing error when total LP expenditure exceeds the selected Game Size budget. Unspent Leader Points are legal.

The permanent Leader Points Configuration entry is an informational tracker. It reports Leader Points remaining / maximum and clamps the displayed remaining value at zero after the budget is spent. The tracker does not itself define legality.

Leader Points are the sole universal Leader-budget mechanism. Do not recreate the retired Counts Toward Leader Maximum category or count-based Leader Capacity validator. Leader-budget legality is expressed through positive LP costs on the correct semantic owner plus shared roster-wide LP overspend validation.

Leader Points are independent of Rare restrictions, pooled faction limits, attachment legality, host attachment capacity, Extra Unit Copy Costs, and other list-building rules. Migrating a selection to LP MUST NOT remove or replace those independent restrictions.

The player-facing rules text for Leader Points MUST use the authoritative Core Rules wording. Custom overspend errors may use concise corrective language appropriate to the listbuilder.


AUTOMATIC CONFIGURATION DUPLICATE TEMPLATE

For catalogue-owned automatic accounting entries that must exist exactly once, suppress the stock max-1 error where practical and use:
"{ENTRY} is automatically managed by the listbuilder and should appear only once. Remove any extra {ENTRY} entries."

If the entry must also be protected against deletion, preserve or separately replace its minimum validation until a constructive missing-entry validator exists.

sharedRules.name: Extra Unit Copy Costs
sharedRules.description: This Configuration item is managed automatically by New Recruit. It displays the extra points added when your roster exceeds the number of identical unit copies that cost their normal points at the selected Game Size. The selected Game Size contains the actual army construction rules and thresholds. Do not add, remove, or edit this accounting item manually.
